title: Associator coherence for the fixed K-flat-normalized system scalar calculus
statement:
Fix the coefficient-derived-system calculus and its K-flat resolution coherence from [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], together with the K-flat normalized closed symmetric tensor structure of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]; this is the fixed calculus and associator used by the scalar-extension tower, not an arbitrary `MonoidalCategory`. For the normalized scalar-extension tower data [def-pur-scalar-extension-tower-data], let $\alpha^{\mathrm{sys},F}$ be the associator of this fixed $F$-coefficient `systemClosed.monoidal` tensor structure. Let $\mathrm{derivedSigma}$ be the unique derived scalar/tensor comparison with the same flat-term K-flat normalization from [stage3-pur-derived-scalar-tensor-normalization]. Define $\sigma^{\mathrm l}$ and $\sigma^{\mathrm r}$ to be the two nested composites of this $\mathrm{derivedSigma}$ in the left- and right-parenthesized scalar extensions of three system objects. Then the fixed system scalar functor satisfies
$$S_{L/E}(\alpha^{\mathrm{sys},E});\sigma^{\mathrm r}=\sigma^{\mathrm l};\alpha^{\mathrm{sys},L}.$$
The associator and both sigma maps are pinned by the common K-flat-normalized tensor model; no completed integral or rational scalar square is asserted here.

source.place: Fixed K-flat-normalized coefficient-system evaluation calculus, closed symmetric tensor, normalized scalar-extension tower and derivedSigma associativity

proof.text: The fixed coefficient-derived-system calculus of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] is the ordinary unbounded derived category of module sheaves on the coefficient sequence ringed site, so [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] applies with $\mathcal O$ the sequence coefficient ring. By the item's hypothesis, $\alpha^{\mathrm{sys},F}$ is the associator of that structure, induced on total tensor complexes of K-flat representatives. Explicitly, for flat-term K-flat complexes $P,Q,R$ over $F$, the complexes $T(P,Q)$ and $T(Q,R)$ are again flat-term K-flat representatives of the derived tensors [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model]. Hence, after the system tensor-model isomorphisms at $(P,Q)$, $(T(P,Q),R)$, $(Q,R)$ and $(P,T(Q,R))$, the map $\alpha^{\mathrm{sys},F}_{QP,QQ,QR}$ is the localization of the native chain associator $a_{P,Q,R}:T(T(P,Q),R)\to T(P,T(Q,R))$.

source.place: The maps used here are tensor reassociation, evaluation, and adjunction units and counits; agent expansion to the fixed coefficient-system calculus.

proof.text: Let $P,Q,R$ be flat-term K-flat complexes over $E$ and $s$ the strict scalar extension of [def-pur-scalar-extension-tower-data]. The pairs $(P,Q)$, $(Q,R)$, $(T(P,Q),R)$ and $(P,T(Q,R))$ consist of flat-term K-flat complexes [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model], and $s$ of each is flat-term K-flat over $L$ [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings-independent]. Apply the `DerivedSigmaModel` equation of [stage3-pur-derived-scalar-tensor-normalization] to these four pairs. Use naturality of $\mathrm{derivedSigma}$ along the $E$ tensor-model isomorphisms and functoriality of the $L$ system tensor. After the tensor-model isomorphisms and the scalar counits $\varepsilon$, $\sigma^{\mathrm l}$ at $(QP,QQ,QR)$ becomes the localization of $\sigma_{T(P,Q),R};(\sigma_{P,Q}\otimes1_{sR})$, and $\sigma^{\mathrm r}$ that of $\sigma_{P,T(Q,R)};(1_{sP}\otimes\sigma_{Q,R})$. Here $\sigma$ is the strict comparison. By Step 1 over $E$ and naturality of $\varepsilon$, $S_{L/E}(\alpha^{\mathrm{sys},E})$ becomes the localization of $s(a^E_{P,Q,R})$. By Step 1 over $L$ for $sP,sQ,sR$, $\alpha^{\mathrm{sys},L}$ becomes that of $a^L_{sP,sQ,sR}$.

source.place: Agent expansion of the normalized scalar/tensor comparison and its associativity on K-flat representatives.

proof.text: It remains to prove the chain identity $s(a^E_{P,Q,R});\sigma_{P,T(Q,R)};(1\otimes\sigma_{Q,R})=\sigma_{T(P,Q),R};(\sigma_{P,Q}\otimes1);a^L_{sP,sQ,sR}$. Take a local homogeneous generator $b\otimes((x\otimes y)\otimes z)$ with $b$ a coefficient section in degree $0$. On the left, the native associator [lem-sf-ringed-tensor-complex-constraints] gives $b\otimes(x\otimes(y\otimes z))$. The generator normalization of $\sigma$ in [def-pur-scalar-extension-tower-data] then gives $(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes(y\otimes z))$ and next $(b\otimes x)\otimes((1\otimes y)\otimes(1\otimes z))$. On the right, $\sigma$ gives $(b\otimes(x\otimes y))\otimes(1\otimes z)$ and then $((b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y))\otimes(1\otimes z)$. The native associator then gives the same element. No Koszul sign occurs, since $b$ and $1$ have degree $0$ and the associator is unsigned. Each term of the strict triple tensor is a direct sum of sheafified tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. A map out of a sheafification is determined on the presheaf tensor, which is generated sectionwise by pure tensors, so the two maps agree in every degree and at every system level. Both sides are already maps of complexes of systems, so no separate check of differentials or quotient transitions is needed.

source.place: Tensor reassociation and coefficient-comparison calculation on homogeneous generators; expanded from the imported blueprint sentence.

proof.text: Localizing Step 3 and inserting the identifications of Step 2 gives the displayed equation at $(QP,QQ,QR)$ for all flat-term K-flat $P,Q,R$. Let $X,Y,Z$ be arbitrary derived system objects represented by complexes $G_X,G_Y,G_Z$. Then [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the sequence ringed site gives flat-term K-flat quasi-isomorphisms $P\to G_X$, $Q\to G_Y$, $R\to G_Z$. These become isomorphisms $u,v,w$ in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Both sides of the equation are composites of natural transformations between functors $D(\mathscr S_E)^3\to D(\mathscr S_L)$: the associators, the natural isomorphism $\mathrm{derivedSigma}$ and its tensor whiskerings, and the functor $S_{L/E}$. Naturality along $(u,v,w)$ therefore writes each side at $(X,Y,Z)$ as the corresponding side at $(QP,QQ,QR)$, conjugated by the invertible maps $S_{L/E}((u\otimes v)\otimes w)$ and $S_{L/E}u\otimes(S_{L/E}v\otimes S_{L/E}w)$. Hence $S_{L/E}(\alpha^{\mathrm{sys},E});\sigma^{\mathrm r}=\sigma^{\mathrm l};\alpha^{\mathrm{sys},L}$ holds for all $X,Y,Z$.
